rubrics.criterion: The query-rendering buffer type no longer owns bind-variable materialization: resolving supplied bind variables (scalars, TUPLE/list expansion, and any custom encoders) into a bound statement, and the missing-bind/type-mismatch error handling, are owned by the parsed-query bound-generation path (or another cohesive owner), not by the buffer that renders AST templates.
rubrics.rationale: Materializing a bound executable query is a distinct concern from rendering a template; this is one of the three responsibilities the buffer absorbed in this case and the one that threads shared mutable state.

rubrics.criterion: The query-rendering buffer type no longer owns literal redaction: replacing literal values with generated bind variables for safe display (with margin comments preserved) is owned by the redaction surface, not by the buffer that renders AST templates.
rubrics.rationale: Redaction-for-display changes for different reasons than rendering (privacy/policy vs. formatting) and was folded onto the buffer; it must be returned to its own owner.

rubrics.criterion: The query-rendering buffer type no longer owns impossible/shadow-query emission: producing the always-empty select/union/default form used to fetch field metadata is owned by the impossible-query surface, not by the buffer that renders AST templates.
rubrics.rationale: Shadow emission is a vtgate/vttablet metadata concern with its own form and lifecycle, distinct from rendering; it must be returned to its own owner.

rubrics.criterion: The bound-generation routine, the bind-variable lookup and value-encoding helpers, the redaction routine, and the impossible-query routine that were reduced to one-line delegations to the buffer are restored to cohesive ownership — each either holds its own logic or delegates to a dedicated owner — while all external call sites remain unchanged in behavior and signature.
rubrics.rationale: Merely relocating concern bodies off the buffer without restoring the natural owners would leave four orphaned pass-throughs; the repair must re-establish ownership at the call-graph edge the injection flattened.

rubrics.criterion: The shared mutable state and configuration added to the rendering buffer only for the absorbed concerns — the bind-variable namespace, the redaction prefix, and the builder setters that install them — no longer reside on the rendering buffer; they live only where the owning concern needs them.
rubrics.rationale: These fields and setters exist solely to support the relocated concerns; leaving them on the buffer would preserve the coupling the repair is meant to remove.

rubrics.criterion: No obsolete injected artifact remains on the rendering buffer after repair — the concern methods, the two added fields, and the builder setters are gone, and the imports added to the buffer solely for the relocated concerns are removed — with no newly unused import left behind in any file and no missing import where the logic now lives.
rubrics.rationale: The injection added imports to the buffer and removed imports from the delegating files; a sound repair must rebalance imports so both files compile without leftover or missing references.

rubrics.criterion: The repair must not alter the bytes of a generated bound query for identical templates and bind variables, including TUPLE/list expansion and custom-encoder output, and must not change the missing-bind or type-mismatch errors raised on the same inputs.
rubrics.rationale: Bound-query output and its error contract are observable behavior relied on by callers and tests; this is the regression most likely when bind-variable materialization is moved.

rubrics.criterion: The repair must not alter the redacted query string — leading margin comments, the statement with literals scrubbed, and trailing margin comments — for any input.
rubrics.rationale: Redaction output is user/log-visible; silently changing the scrubbed text or comment framing would be a behavior regression independent of the bound-query path.

rubrics.criterion: The repair must not alter the impossible/shadow query text produced for select, union, and default node forms, including the always-false predicate and group-by passthrough.
rubrics.rationale: The shadow query's shape is what makes a select return zero rows for field metadata; any change risks breaking vtgate/vttablet metadata fetches.

rubrics.criterion: The repair must not change any public signature of the bound-generation, bind-variable-lookup, value-encoding, redaction, or impossible-query entry points, and must not cause the package test suite to fail.
rubrics.rationale: These entry points are the compatibility contract for callers across the parser and downstream tooling; signature changes or test regressions would make a structurally-correct repair unusable.
